blocks.text: Multiple FROM stages let you compile in a fat builder and copy only the artifacts into a slim runtime, so compilers, headers and caches never ship.

blocks.code:
FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS builder
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends build-essential && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/pip pip install -r requirements.txt

FROM python:3.12-slim-bookworm AS runtime
ENV PATH=/opt/venv/bin:$PATH
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
COPY app /app/app
USER 10001
CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

blocks.src: generate: Builder stage (compilers, headers, pip cache, /opt/venv) with an arrow "COPY --from=builder /opt/venv" into a runtime stage (slim base + venv + app)
blocks.alt: Only artifacts cross the stage boundary.
blocks.caption: Only artifacts cross the stage boundary.

items: Copy the venv to the same path: console scripts have absolute shebangs.
Same Python minor version and libc in both stages (ABI).
Shared libs don't travel with the venv: install libpq5 etc. in runtime.
The last stage is the default target: put runtime last or always use `--target`.

blocks.text: Q: "What does a multi-stage build buy you, and what breaks when copying a venv between stages?" A: "A small runtime without build tooling. The venv must land at the same path, with the same Python version and libc, and runtime shared libraries like libpq5 must be installed separately."

items: Same path, same Python, same libc.
